newsitem.title: FRANCE: France proposes international Zaire operation.
newsitem.headline: France proposes international Zaire operation.

text.p: France urged the United States, Europe and Africa on Monday into urgent talks on how to restore security in eastern Zaire and help avert disaster for more than one million civilians fleeing fighting.
Foreign Minister Herve de Charette indicated a possible international operation would only be temporary and would allow refugees to return to their camps and villagers to return home.

"France proposes to its partners, particularly the Organisation of African Unity, Europe, the United States and Canada to hold without further delay a meeting to discuss how to organise possible ways of temporarily establishing security in north and south Kivu," de Charette said.

More than one million refugees, mostly Rwandan Hutus, caught in fighting between Zairean forces and Tutsi rebels backed by Rwanda's Tutsi army have fled camps and been left without food after the departure of aid organisations.
De Charette, reading out a statement to reporters, also called for a meeting of the U.N. Security Council to speed up the organisation of an international peace conference on the region.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said France was now awaiting its partners' reply. "The ball is in their court," he told reporters.
East and Central African states are due to meet in Nairobi on Tuesday to discuss the situation in Zaire.
A French cabinet minister at the weekend urged France's European partners to be prepared to intervene to avert a humanitarian disaster.

France, which has some troops in various African countries, single-handedly intervened in eastern Zaire and Rwanda in 1994 to stop killings after the Rwanda genocide, but does not appear willing to intervene again without a clear international mandate.
Paris is still smarting from charges from African countries and some of its own partners that it intervened mostly to advance French policy objectives.
